title: Same Request. Different Caches. Different Savings.

data.kicker: LLM cost cheat sheet · 6 caching layers
title: Same Request.
Different Caches.
Different Savings.

intro.before: A lot of LLM traffic repeats: the same prompts, prefixes, documents and tool calls. Caching decides
intro.highlight: what you never pay for twice
intro.after: , at each layer of the stack.

bullets.text: Hashes the full prompt; repeats return instantly
Zero model cost on a hit
Deterministic and easy to invalidate
Misses any rewording, even one character
Reuses answers above a similarity threshold
Catches paraphrased repeat questions
Big savings on FAQ-style traffic
A loose threshold serves wrong answers
Provider stores the processed prompt prefix
Cached input tokens billed at a discount
Faster first token on long prompts
Exact prefixes only; entries expire
Stores attention keys and values per token
New tokens attend to the cache only
Avoids recomputing the prefix each step
Memory grows with context length and batch
Stores vectors keyed by a hash of the text
Re-indexing skips unchanged documents
Cuts embedding spend and indexing time
A new embedding model means re-embed all
Caches tool or API results by arguments
Agents stop repeating the same calls
A TTL keeps results reasonably fresh
Stale answers if the TTL is too long

principles.sub: A cache that rarely hits only adds latency; log hits, misses and savings.
System prompt, tools and documents first; the user's question last.
Too loose serves wrong answers; test on real paraphrases and near-misses.

rows.q: Long shared system prompt or docs
Long outputs on your own GPUs

quote.big: The cheapest token is the one you never compute.
quote.small: Cache what repeats; measure what hits.
